text: At the Tavrin Valley cooperative on Tuesday, farm manager Elio Varn said the sugar beet crop failed outright this season after weeks of erratic frost and a late dry spell. Standing beside a line of split, undersized roots, Varn told the Gazette he had expected a modest harvest in early September, but “there was nothing left worth lifting” by the first week of October. He said the co-op planted 186 hectares of sugar beet in April, and fewer than 12 hectares produced marketable weight. Workers I spoke with said the factory trucks had already been cancelled. The cooperative now plans to switch part of the land to barley and clover next spring.
